files.label: marts.dim_postcode_geo
files.description: Postcode -> ABS geography rollups (SA2 / SA3 / SA4 / Greater-Capital / state), one row per postcode, from the postcode_geo seed (ABS 2016 correspondences). The geo dimension the Explore profiler and the agent use to roll a postcode up to a region: the sales/rent/yield marts carry only postcode, so "rent by SA3" or "top-yield SA4" joins through here on postcode. Shared across the property datasets (readable with ANY property grant). Verified by not_null/unique on postcode.

files.label: marts.property_rent
files.description: Aggregate mart for cleaned NSW rental bond lodgements. Physical table: marts.property_rent, matching raw.property_rent and staging.property_rent for easy lineage. One row per (postcode, property_type, bedroom_band, month). Rent source data has no suburb, so the honest aggregate grain is postcode-level. Holds cleaned attributes plus additive aggregate metrics so consumers can re-aggregate to higher levels and compute derived metrics such as rent growth or joined yield in SQL. No precomputed ALL rows or growth percentages. Belongs to the `nsw_rent` dataset (RLS-scoped). Verified by assert_property_rent_has_coverage and assert_property_rent_unique_postcode_type_bedroom_month.

files.label: marts.property_sales
files.description: Aggregate mart for cleaned NSW residential sales. Physical table: marts.property_sales, matching raw.property_sales and staging.property_sales for easy lineage. One row per (postcode, suburb, property_type, area_band, zoning, month). Holds cleaned attributes plus additive aggregate metrics so consumers can re-aggregate to higher levels and compute derived metrics such as growth or yield in SQL. No precomputed ALL rows, growth percentages, or joined rent metrics. Belongs to the `nsw_sales` dataset (RLS-scoped). Verified by assert_property_sales_has_coverage and assert_property_sales_unique_postcode_suburb_type_band_zoning_month.

files.label: marts.property_yield
files.description: Gross rental yield by (postcode, property_type, month) — sales JOIN rent, the combined view neither single-source mart can answer, at the same month grain as property_sales and property_rent. Physical table: marts.property_yield. Ported from docs/chronicle/property_yield_20241003.py. Keeps the additive components (total_sale_value, n_sold, total_weekly_rent, n_rented) so a consumer re-aggregating to quarter, year, SA3 or across property types can recompute averages and yield; gross_yield_pct is a derived ratio-of-averages (52 * avg_weekly_rent / avg_sale_price * 100), not an average of per-row yields. Thin cells are floored per month at n_sold >= 5 and n_rented >= 5. Belongs to the `nsw_yield` dataset (its own RLS grant). Verified by assert_property_yield_has_coverage and assert_property_yield_range.

files.label: staging.int_postcode_geo
files.description: Postcode <-> suburb bridge: every (postcode, suburb) pair seen in the sale records, with a sale count. Does NOT collapse to one suburb per postcode — postcode <-> suburb is not 1:1, so every locality is present. Use it to resolve a suburb name to its postcode(s), especially for rent questions: marts.property_rent has no suburb (raw.property_rent has no locality), so "rent in <suburb>" means looking the suburb up here to get its postcode(s), then querying rent by postcode. Belongs to the `nsw_sales` dataset (RLS-scoped, since it's derived from sales).

files.label: staging.property_rent
files.description: Record-grain NSW rental bond lodgements. Physical table: staging.property_rent, matching raw.property_rent and marts.property_rent for easy lineage. One row per bond, cleaned and typed from raw.property_rent (all 5 raw columns are used; nothing was left out). Same role as staging.property_sales — the clean mirror of raw.property_rent. Most questions are better answered by marts.property_rent; use this table for record-level questions raw.property_rent's own columns can answer, e.g. "2-bedroom vs 3-bedroom rent in a suburb". Always filter by postcode and/or rent_month first — this table is ~3M rows. Belongs to the `nsw_rent` dataset (RLS-scoped).

files.label: staging.property_sales
files.description: Record-grain NSW residential sales. Physical table: staging.property_sales, matching raw.property_sales and marts.property_sales for easy lineage. One row per sale, cleaned and typed from raw.property_sales (dates parsed, postcode normalised, non-market transfers filtered, house/unit derived). This is the clean, verified mirror of raw.property_sales, kept as wide as relevant rather than a curated subset. Most questions are better answered by marts.property_sales (a precomputed aggregate) — use this table only when a question is genuinely about individual records or a metric the marts don't carry: "top 10 addresses by sale price in a suburb", "average price by lot size band", "list sales over $2M in a postcode". Always filter by postcode and/or sale_month first — this table is ~3M rows. Belongs to the `nsw_sales` dataset (RLS-scoped). Verified by the marts.property_sales dbt tests indirectly (built from this table).

tools.name: extract
tools.description: Run a governed SELECT; the result is loaded as a pandas DataFrame `name`.
tools.guardrail: sql_guardrails + RLS — governed SELECT through the read-only agent_ro role

tools.name: run_analysis
tools.description:
Execute pandas over the extracted frame(s) in the sandbox; calls skills.*.

Assign the finished report to `result` (skills.build_report(...)). Returns the skills used on success, or the error to fix. Prefer skills; if none fits you MAY use pandas but MUST call skills.skill_gap(need, why).
tools.guardrail: sandbox (pyodide) — isolated pandas execution, skills.* preferred

tools.name: lookup_values
tools.description:
Resolve exact distinct values of a text column (e.g. a name's casing). FREE.

Pass the schema-qualified table the column lives in (see the mart index / schema/<table>.md). Dataset-agnostic — no default table. Resolve SEVERAL values in ONE call with `|` alternation (e.g. pattern="Normanhurst|Hornsby"); matching is case-insensitive contains, so plain words work — never retry with different casing.

tools.name: no_answer
tools.description:
Declare that the available marts can't answer this question.

Use when no dataset covers what's asked (wrong domain, missing metric or dimension). Records an honest reason instead of forcing a misleading report. Give a short, user-facing reason (what's missing / what the data does cover). Then return a one-line confirmation.

tools.name: start_deck
tools.description:
Open the answer's Google Slides deck and its backing Sheet. Call ONCE, after your analysis is done and before the first add_slide.

Give a short deck title naming the question's subject.
tools.guardrail: Google Sheets/Slides via the service's own OAuth credential — the only third-party egress; never sandbox code; public sharing gated by DECK_PUBLIC

tools.name: add_slide
tools.description:
Append one slide to the deck, filling it in a single atomic write.

`layout` must be an exact name from layouts.md (Grep it first). Pass `frame` to chart or tabulate a frame you already extracted — the rows are written to the Sheet and the chart is NATIVE and editable, not a picture. `headline` is the slide title; `commentary` is one or two sentences on what the numbers mean, not what they show. Use `columns` to pick and order which of the frame's columns to plot; the first is the x axis / label column, which must be unique per row for a chart — aggregate first, or pass a categorical second column and it is pivoted into series automatically. On a KPI layout, `kpi` is the number itself and the optional `kpi_label` says what it measures (e.g. 'median sale price'). The footer and the source line are filled in for you.
tools.guardrail: layout name must be in the curated catalogue (layouts.md); one atomic batchUpdate per slide

tools.name: Read
tools.description: Read one file in the run workspace (CLAUDE.md, marts.md, layouts.md, schema/*.md, knowledge/*.md, frames/*.head.csv).
